purpose: How the reference shorts HANDLE each situation (camera, cuts, light, colour, characters, props, effects, physics, script-to-picture). Habits to learn from, not shots to copy. Single source of truth: kit/docs/PLAYBOOK.md is generated from this file by kit/tools/build_playbook.py. Numbers come from kit/reference/study/*.json (measured) and kit/reference/db/*.json. STATUS: the render code does NOT read this file. Only the Gemini prompt (tools/gen_api.py) includes the generated PLAYBOOK.md, and that is untested. A rule here is knowledge, not an engine feature, until it is listed as implemented under 'engine' below.

confidence_key.measured: computed from every frame of the reference videos by kit/tools/ref_study.py or ref_measure.py
confidence_key.seen: read by eye from frame sheets / full-size frames / 0.1 s strips; times are given as evidence
confidence_key.inferred: reasoned from what was seen; check against the next references before trusting
confidence_key.proposed: designed by an independent study (ChatGPT, sampled frames at 2 fps); NOT measured or seen by us; treat as a starting value and test it before trusting

units.speed: peak flight speed is stored in px per frame at 270 px frame width. Multiply by 11.1 for percent of frame width per second (9.85 px = 109 %/s).
units.luma: 0 black .. 1 white, mean over the frame without the caption band
units.palette: number of 4-bit colour bins holding more than 0.5 % of the picture

limits: 17 camera-studied videos, all in one house style (3D world, 2D bean-head cards, one-word captions). Another genre may need other values.
Topic groups (history/war 6, money-gamble-crime 6, engineering 3, science-mind 1, night-horror 1) are Claude's labels. PRELIMINARY: groups of 1 to 3 are single examples, not ranges.

Scene counter: precision 0.84, recall 0.84 on 43 changes labelled by eye in 4 videos (first 30 s). Type labels: 5 of 6 spot checks right. Treat counts as about +-20 %. Angle changes inside a scene are not counted as scene changes.
3 of the videos (vp3, vp4, vp5) are 360x640; the rest 720x1280. Our v2.1 is 1080x1920. All measures are ratios.

Head finder works on clean near-white heads only; eyes are measured only where open dots are visible; limb thickness separate from outline, body proportions, material types and physics trajectories are NOT measured (no reliable way from a flat video).
Caption text height is reliable in 8 of 17 videos (single word in a clean band); the rest are inflated by white scenery.
Sound: only loudness (-14 LUFS) and onset alignment (none beyond chance) are known. Music, voice and sound effects cannot be separated from the mixed track.
The 6 older reference videos are in the colour database but NOT in the camera study (their video files were not kept).
No script text for the references. Script-to-picture rules come from reading the captions on the frames.
These rules are NOT read by the render code. They reach Gemini only through the PLAYBOOK in its prompt (untested).
Rules with conf "proposed" (15 rules, merged 2026-11-08 from an independent ChatGPT study) were not measured or seen by us and have not been applied in a video yet.

faults: 58 hard cuts per minute, references 2 to 15 (median 7)
scene changes 28.3 per minute, references 16.0-24.9 (median 20.4): ours changes place somewhat too often (about 40 % above the median)
every scene change is a hard cut (100 %); references: 43 % dissolve, 22 % camera fly-through, 21 % hard cut, 12 % in-place, 2 % whip
25 hard cuts per minute are angle cuts inside one scene; references median 1.1 per minute
78 % of shots are a pure zoom (push-in), references 0 to 7 %
the same camera move repeats in the next shot 89 % of the time, references 0 to 63 % (median 33 %)
camera moves are flat (parallax 0.27, references 0.32 to 0.44)
flights are short (0.57 s, references 0.8 to 1.6 s) and the pauses between them are long (2.3 s, references 0.7 to 1.7 s)
picture moves fast only 21 % of the time (references 27 to 54 %)
surfaces: 60 % flat colour and 5.6 % gradient, references 35-48 % flat and 14-20 % gradient
palette 23 colours (references 36 to 46); frame-to-frame change 0.6 to 2.6 (references 3.6 to 9.5)
no captions in the picture (references: one word at a time, 100 % of the time)

rules.rule: The camera is almost always alive, but not always flying.
do: Plan each beat as HOLD or FLIGHT. Flights run 27-54 % of the time, slow creep or stillness 20-51 %. The mix depends on the topic (see PRF-02).
Never leave a long beat with a frozen camera and nothing else moving.
rules.ours_now: fast 21 %, still 43 %

rules.rule: A flight is about one second long, one every 3 seconds, followed by a short hold.
do: Flight length 0.5-2.8 s, typical 1.1 s.
One flight every 2-5 s (13-24 per minute).
Hold between flights typically 0.7-1.7 s.
Peak speed about 100 % of frame width per second (45-245).
rules.ours_now: flight 0.57 s, pause 2.3 s

rules.rule: Move the camera through the 3D world. Do not just zoom.
do: Every flight changes camera POSITION: orbit 20-60 degrees, crane up or down, dolly past objects, tilt while pushing.
Foreground, subject and background must slide at different speeds (parallax).
A pure push-in or pull-out with no pan, tilt or orbit is rare: use it for 0-7 % of shots.

numbers.shot_net_motion: shots that combine a push or pull with a pan, tilt or orbit make up about 90 % of all shots (80-100 %)

evidence: pirate_cannonballs 0-1.2 s (orbit around the cannon, sea and island revealed)
memory_price 4-7 s (fly down an alley into the shop)
rules.ours_now: 78 % pure push-in, parallax 0.27

rules.rule: REVEAL: start tight on a detail or a face, then fly out, up or around until the place or its size is clear.
do: Frame 1: face or small object. Last frame: wide view with the hero object of the topic in it.
Use crane-up or top-down to show layout or scale of a system.
evidence: town_button 4-7 s (crane up to a top view of the circular town)

rules.rule: LAND ON THE PROP: a fast push toward the named prop that slows down as it arrives, timed to the word.
do: Start 0.3-0.5 s before the word, arrive on the word.
End with the prop filling 40-100 % of the frame, readable.
Ease: fast start, slow finish (decelerate).
evidence: second_draw 14-15 s (push to the gun while yellow streaks fly)
town_button 23-25 s (button under the glass dome)

rules.rule: Power and danger: low angle, big object in the foreground.
do: Camera at ground height looking slightly up, holster or weapon or hull edge large and sharp in the lower third, subject behind.
evidence: second_draw 0-4 s (bullet and holster in the foreground, camera tilts up to the face)

rules.rule: FOLLOW: when something travels, the camera pans or tracks with it and the background streams by.
do: Keep the mover in the same screen spot, let the background slide, constant speed.

rules.rule: Dialogue and reaction beats are HELD: two-shot or close-up, slow creep, 1.5-4 s.
do: Save the fast flights for reveals and impacts.
Change only the faces and small props while the camera rests.
evidence: second_draw 9-13 s (four seconds on one medium shot)

rules.rule: Ease every flight. Half are steady, a quarter ease in and out.
do: constant speed 50 % of flights (follow, long gentle drift)
ease in and out 23 % (reveals)
decelerate 8 % (landing on a prop)
move then hold 7 %, varying 10 %
almost never accelerate
rules.ours_now: 67 % constant, 22 % ease, 11 % accelerate

rules.rule: Do not repeat the same move beat after beat. Vary push, pull, orbit, tilt, pan, top-down, low angle, first person.
do: Never more than two beats in a row with the same kind of move.
Change camera height or angle at least every 2-3 s of flight time.
rules.ours_now: 89 % repeat

rules.rule: Use shot size as a language: tiny people in a wide world, medium two-shots, face close-ups, extreme close-ups of props.
do: Wide: people under 10 % of frame height, the world is the subject.
Medium: people 35-50 % of frame height.
Close-up: head 40-60 % of frame width.
Insert: prop fills the frame.
Change size at nearly every sentence.

rules.rule: Frame with something blurred in the foreground at an edge (rope, pole, rail, mast, leaves) to build depth.
do: One soft foreground object on one side, subject sharp behind it.

rules.rule: Hard cuts are rare: a few per minute. The camera and dissolves carry most scene changes (see CUT-02).
do: 2-15 hard cuts per minute, median 7.
Do not cut just to change the angle: fly the camera instead.
Use a hard cut for a new place, a new time, or a change of topic.

numbers.long_takes: vp3: 0 hard cuts in 45 s, yet 13 scene changes made by dissolves and fly-throughs (see CUT-02)

rules.ours_now: 58 per minute

rules.rule: Carry the viewer to the next beat with the camera: fly through, into or under the next place. Do NOT add heavy blur: measured sharpness at the flight peak is the same as at a hold.
do: End a flight pointing at the next location, start the next beat already moving.
Motion blur is at most slight: sharpness at flight peak / median sharpness is 0.89-1.20 (median 1.05).
evidence: memory_price 4-8 s (alley, light-lined corridor, shop interior in one move)

rules.rule: Cross-dissolve 4-10 frames, with a ghost of the old picture, for memory, thought, time shift or a change of speaker.
do: Overlap both pictures at 50 % for 2-3 frames.
evidence: memory_price 42-46 s (ghost of the hooded buyer over the boy)
second_draw 13.6 s (dissolve to the quick-draw man)

rules.rule: Round masks: spyglass circle on black for looking at something far, round windows as frames, a black circle closing as an eye.
do: Use rarely, once or twice per short, for a view-through or a turning point.
evidence: second_draw 44-53 s (black circle, then round windows)

rules.rule: Smoke or cloud wipe: a puff fills the frame, the next place is behind it.
do: Smoke grows over 6-10 frames, clears into the new scene.
evidence: pirate_cannonballs 17.5-18.5 s (cannon smoke to open sea)

rules.rule: End with a callback: return to the first place or object, changed.
do: Last shot repeats the opening place or prop, with the final idea visible on it.
evidence: second_draw 54-55 s (street scene like the opening)
town_button 64-65 s (crowd around the button from the first shot)

rules.rule: Every frame has a deep shadow and a near-white highlight. Mean brightness is 0.30-0.54 for most stories, down to 0.23 for a dark-room mind story.
do: Darkest 2 % of pixels 0.07-0.15, brightest 2 % 0.84-0.98, contrast std 0.16-0.25.
Night is not dim: lamps, windows and moon are bright, the subject is lit.

numbers.brightness_video_median: 0.23-0.62 over 17 videos (p10-p90 0.30-0.54); day war/engineering about 0.5, night or mind stories 0.23-0.38

rules.ours_now: mean 0.37, but flat

rules.rule: One dominant colour family per place, with warm against cool.
do: Night: navy and purple with warm lamp and window pools.
Day: saturated blue sky, orange or sand ground.
Sunset: orange glow, long violet shadows.
Indoors: warm lamp pool on cool walls.
Pick the family before building the set.
evidence: memory_price 5-15 s (blue street, yellow shop windows)
roller_coasters 16-28 s (moonlit blue, warm lanterns and lights)

rules.rule: Colour follows feeling. Change the grade at the emotional turn.
do: Sad, ill, lonely: cold blue, low key light.
Warm memory, joy: golden hour, soft glow.
Danger, duel: low orange sun, hard long shadows.
Power, shock: bright yellow streaks or rim light.
evidence: memory_price 32-45 s (blue hospital against the golden lake)

rules.rule: Use light effects as scenery: bloom on lamps, windows and sun; god rays through glass; sun glare in the sky; rim light on night characters; string lights; wet-street reflections and rain streaks at night.
do: At least one light effect in every wide shot.
evidence: town_button 23-25 s (beams through the glass dome)

rules.rule: The reference picture has 38-47 colours and soft gradients. Flat colour with an outline gives 23. Add gradient, texture and light, not more coloured boxes.
do: Sky gradient with soft clouds that have a shaded underside.
Ground and walls with grain, stones, tufts.
Atmosphere: haze that turns far things bluer and lighter.
Bloom and soft shading with 3-4 steps plus ambient occlusion in corners.
rules.ours_now: palette 23, v2.1 added coloured props and palette did not rise

rules.rule: Each place: 6-10 dressing pieces plus one HERO object or shape that is the topic.
do: Canyon wall with coloured strata for a railroad story, one giant loop for a roller-coaster story, a plaza of rings with a button under glass for the button story, a ship deck with cannons and barrels for the cannonball story.

rules.rule: Surfaces have real texture.
do: Rail ballast as single stones with highlights, sleepers, steel rail with gloss.
Sand with pebbles and grass tufts, wood planks with grain and nails.
Tile plaza with ring pattern, checker floor, brick.
Grass as many thin blades, water with caustics and foam, glass with highlights.

rules.rule: Three depth layers: soft foreground, sharp middle, hazy background with silhouettes (islands, hills, skyline, ships).
do: Put a far landmark in every wide shot.

rules.rule: Outline: thin dark ink on the silhouettes of props and structures. No line on sky, water, clouds, ground joins.
do: Characters keep the thickest line.

rules.rule: Crowds are real: hundreds of tiny people with different hats and colours in stands and streets, and a few larger ones in front.
do: Rows rising in height, flags and bunting, a few people animated.

rules.rule: Character anatomy: big near-white head, bean body with real clothing details, thin noodle limbs.
do: Head: circle slightly wider than tall, soft warm-grey shade on the lower rim, thick uneven near-black outline about 3-4 % of head width.
Body: bean as tall as the head, with pocket, buttons, medals or braid, belt, collar, prints (flowers, stripes, dots).
Arms: thin lines about as long as the body, small round hands.
Legs: very thin, 1.3-1.8 times the body, no feet.
Whole figure about 3.5 head heights.
evidence: frames memory_price 20.5 s, perfect_railroads 18.2 s, second_draw 15.5 s, town_button 11.2 s, roller_coasters 5.2 s, storm_oil 10.2 s

rules.rule: Identity from headwear and clothes: bowler, chef hat, striped cap, cowboy hat, bandana, tricorn, top hat, police cap.
do: One hat shape and one colour per role, kept in every shot.
Hats move with the head and fly off when the body is hit.

rules.rule: Lit by the scene: skin takes a warm or cool tint, soft gradient, soft contact shadow on the ground.
do: No flat white paper-cut look.
evidence: memory_price 50-54 s (warm lamp on the face)

rules.rule: Characters hold props with their noodle arms and touch the set (ladle, hammer, telescope, mug, cane, gun, pole).
do: Every character in a medium shot holds or touches something.

rules.rule: Tiny face, strong emotion language.
do: Eyes: white ring with outline and dot pupil, or plain dots. Eyebrows: thick short strokes, they carry the feeling.
Mouth: line, smirk, open D, teeth grid. Extras: moustache strokes.
In close-ups change the expression every 1-1.5 s.

rules.rule: Emotion vocabulary with effects drawn on or around the head.
do: Anger: head turns purple, white steam puffs on both sides, V brows, gritted teeth.
Fear: wide ring eyes, 2-3 sweat drops, teeth grid.
Shock: yellow glowing irises, vein mark, speed streaks.
Smug: half-closed eyes, smirk.
Knocked out: face-down, hat off, X or spiral eyes.
Joy: closed arc eyes, big smile.
Sick: pale, tired eyes.

rules.rule: The key idea of the story is a readable prop with text or numbers.
do: Odometer counter (BAHAMAS 0299), gauge (HAPPINESS needle and glow), odds board (MILK RUN 100-1), banner (OPENING TOMORROW), ledger (YEAR 2025 SOLD stamps), stopwatch, newspaper headline, polaroid.
Text unlit and spelled the same every time.

rules.rule: A prop appears in frame within about 0.3 s of the word that names it, and its label can repeat the word.
do: Barrel labelled GARBAGE while the narrator says garbage; barrel LANGRAGE while he explains langrage.

rules.rule: Numbers move with the story: the needle swings, the glow grows, the ledger fills with SOLD stamps year after year.
do: Animate the value over 1-2 s on the beat it changes.

rules.rule: Motifs: one recurring character or object (frog badge, hooded buyer, red button) returns at least three times, each time in a new light.
do: Reuse the exact model and colour.

rules.rule: Draw the idea inside the world: glowing ring with chalk arcs and numbers, blackboard with a sketch, map.
do: Use when the script explains a mechanism or counts something.

rules.rule: Anticipation, action, follow-through.
do: Smash: hold the raised hammer at least 0.6 s, hit, the object bulges for 1-2 frames, bursts into pieces within 0.2 s, pieces and coins keep flying 0.5-1 s.
The bystander reacts within 0.2 s.

rules.rule: Impact starburst: radial spiky shards in 2-3 layers, smoke puff, flying splinters that spread for about 0.8 s, hole shows what is behind.
do: Cut or push to the impact point, then pull back to show the crowd reacting.

rules.rule: Speed streaks: bright yellow vertical streaks, flying pebbles and dust around a fast draw or jump, with a quick push-in.
do: Streaks for 0.5-1 s, camera ends on the weapon or hand.

rules.rule: Always a few particles: dust, pebbles, rain, confetti, coins, smoke puffs, steam, sparks, bubbles, floating motes.
do: Particles move in every wide and action shot.

rules.rule: Things have weight.
do: Debris follows gravity arcs and spins, hats fly and fall, bodies fall with rotation then lie still, barrels roll, a cannon recoils, a horse gallops with a rider bob, camera tracks the mover.

rules.rule: Comedy: a visual gag after a hard beat (a knocked-out man whose face is stamped in the sand ring), exaggerated reaction faces, size contrast.
do: Hold the gag shot 1-1.5 s.

rules.rule: One idea per sentence, one picture per idea. New place or angle at every sentence, new face or prop at every clause.
do: Narration runs about 2.5-3 words a second, captions show 1-3 words.

rules.rule: Show every important noun. Turn abstract ideas into an object: memory = ticket and shelves of boxes, happiness = gauge, time = ledger of years, rules = a button under glass.
do: List the nouns of each sentence before planning the shot and check each one appears.

rules.rule: Hook in the first 2-3 seconds: a face reacts, the main prop or place is in frame, and the first flight starts within the first second.
do: First fast flight starts at frame 1-27 (0.03-0.9 s) in 7 of 8 references; 2 of them start at frame 1-3.

rules.rule: Story shape: hook, set up the world with a reveal flight, escalate with a new place every 3-6 s, twist or payoff with a gag, callback ending.
do: Plan the shot list in these five blocks.

rules.rule: Captions: bold white, thick black outline, centred at about 70 % of frame height, 1-3 words at a time, changing with the voice.
do: Keep the caption band free of important detail.

rules.rule: Final loudness about -14 LUFS, loudness range 1.7-3.2 LU.
do: Master to -14 LUFS.

rules.rule: The PLACE or set-up changes about every 2.4 seconds (18-24 times a minute). Four of every five scene changes are made WITHOUT a hard cut.
rules.why: Fast change of place keeps attention. A fly-through or a dissolve changes the place while the viewer's eye stays with the moving picture, so it feels smooth, not choppy.
do: Change scene every 2-3 s, 18-24 times per minute.
Make the change with: dissolve (43 % of changes), camera fly-through (22 %), hard cut (21 %), in-place change (12 %), whip (2 %).
Keep the camera moving inside the scene; do not cut for a new angle (see CUT-03).

numbers.scene_changes_per_min: p10 18.34 / median 20.4 / p90 23.64 (min 16.0, max 24.9); mean over videos 20.9
numbers.counter_accuracy: precision 0.84, recall 0.84 against 43 hand-labelled changes in 4 videos (first 30 s)

rules.ours_now: 28 per minute, all hard cuts

rules.rule: Do not cut to a new angle inside the same scene. Stay in the place and move the camera.
rules.why: The references hold one world for about 2 s and fly through it; every extra cut inside the scene breaks the 3D space the viewer just understood.
do: Hard cuts inside one scene: about 1 per minute at most (references median 1.1).
A hard cut must land on a NEW place or a new beat of the script, never just a new angle of the same set.
rules.ours_now: 25 per minute inside scenes

rules.rule: Most scene changes are either a fly-through (the camera passes into the next place) or a short cross-dissolve where both places show for a moment.
rules.why: Both keep the picture moving across the change, so the viewer does not feel a jump.
do: Dissolve when the next place is far away in space or time: the old picture ghosts through the new one for about 0.2-0.4 s (6-12 frames, read on 0.1 s strips).
Fly-through when the next place is next door: the camera ends pointing at a door, street or panel, and the next shot starts already moving.
evidence: vp3 10 s, 16 s, 24 s (dissolves between prize hall, counter and street)
random_numbers 10-11 s (ghost of the tower over the office)
vp3 2-5 s (neon street seen from above, camera drops to the door)

rules.rule: WHEN NOT TO MOVE: hold the camera when a person talks, thinks, reacts, or when a number or a rule is being read.
rules.why: The viewer needs a steady frame to read a face, a caption or a number. Moving the camera there competes with the information.
do: Hold 2-6 s (up to 10 s once) on one medium shot or close-up.
Keep life in the frame while the camera rests: eyes, mouth, small gestures, light flicker, floating particles, a slow creep of 1-3 %.
Move again at the next scene change or the next reveal.
evidence: idea_zone 0-10 s (one character on a chair under a lamp, almost still)
random_numbers 15-23 s (clerk beside the elevator panel)
vp4 3-8 s (clerk and customer at the counter)

rules.rule: CUTAWAY: show hidden things (underground, inside a body, deep water) as a sliced side view with a scale or gauge.
rules.why: A side slice shows layers and depth at once, so one picture explains where things are.
do: Cut the world like a cake: soil layers with a coffin under the grass, the character as a see-through body with the brain and nerves glowing, an underwater column with a depth gauge and level labels.
Label the layers in the world itself, in big letters.
evidence: grave_bell 4-9 s (grass, soil layers, coffin, rope up to the bell)
idea_zone 24-27 s (sleep depth as underwater gauge)

rules.rule: UNIVERSAL for every topic (stable across all 17 videos): scene pace, depth parallax, colour richness, surface mix.
rules.why: These values barely move between a war story, a lottery story and a sleep story, so they are the house style, not a topic choice.
do: Scene change every 2-3 s (18-24 per minute).
Camera parallax 0.32-0.44.
Palette 36-46 colours, saturation 0.39-0.57, edge detail 0.11-0.22.
Flat colour at most 48 % of the picture, gradient 14-20 %.
Pure zoom shots at most 7 %.

rules.rule: TOPIC DECIDES how busy the camera is. Action and machines: flying about half the time. Talk, tricks and money: holding about half the time.
rules.why: Moving objects (armies, coasters, trains) give the camera things to follow; talk and number stories need steady frames to read.
do: history_war, engineering: fast 45-51 % of time, still 24-27 %, frame change 7.5-7.6.
money_gamble_crime: fast 30 %, still 49 %, frame change 4.8.
Pick the profile from the topic, then keep scene pace and parallax from PRF-01.
evidence: topic_profiles.json; the grouping into topics is my label, group sizes 3 to 6

rules.rule: MOOD decides brightness. Day stories sit near 0.5, night and mind stories go down to 0.23-0.38 but keep bright accents.
rules.why: The dark rooms and nights in the references stay readable because lamps, neon, windows and glows are the brightest, and the characters are lit.
do: Dark mood: set the ambient low, add one strong motivated light (lamp cone, neon, moon, candle) and keep the character face near white.
Day mood: sky and ground bright, shadows blue or purple, not black.

numbers.night_mind_range: 0.23 idea_zone, 0.28 vp3 neon night, 0.31 memory_price, 0.36 grave_bell

evidence: idea_zone 0-10 s (lamp cone on a dark room)
grave_bell 10-20 s (blue snow night, warm lit windows)

rules.rule: MONEY, GAMBLING and NUMBER stories carry the idea on a big object with numbers: a register, a counter, a panel of lights, a scoreboard, a ticket.
rules.why: The audience reads the number once and understands the stake; the prop makes the data physical.
do: Build one hero number prop per story: large, high contrast, readable at phone size.
Let it change on the spoken word (counter rolls, light turns on, ticket value appears).
Put a bright, saturated, crowded place around it (neon, carpet, shelves) so the number prop stands out by being clean.
evidence: vp5 7-8 s (YEARS AT WAR counter rolls 099 to 100)
random_numbers 14-24 s (elevator panel of numbered lights)
vp3 5-8 s (endless row of machines in perspective)

rules.observed: Scene changes in 17 references: 43 % dissolve, 22 % camera fly-through, 21 % hard cut, 12 % in-place (prop or flash), 2 % whip. Ours: 100 % hard cut.
rules.rule: Mix the ways of changing scene. Dissolve is the default, a fly-through is the second choice, a hard cut is a choice for a new topic or a surprise.
rules.why: The viewer keeps one continuous moving picture; a hard cut every 2 s feels like a slideshow.
do: Per minute (median video): about 9 dissolves, 5-6 camera fly-throughs, 3-4 hard cuts, 2 in-place changes, 0 whips (whip is rare: 0-2 per minute).
Dissolve = 6-12 frames. Fly-through = the camera enters a door, tunnel, window, furnace, panel or street that is the next place.
In-place = the prop or light changes while the camera rests (flash, turning a page, light switching on).
rules.ours_now: 100 % hard cut

rules.observed: Camera flights start already moving (about 40 % of peak speed in the first tenth), reach the peak about 38 % of the way through, then taper slowly. Ramp-up 0.28 s, ramp-down 0.47 s.
rules.rule: Shape every camera flight with a quick attack and a long, soft release.
rules.why: A fast start keeps energy; a long ease-out lets the viewer land on the new framing.
do: Speed curve for a flight, 11 points from start to end as a share of peak speed: 0.39, 0.56, 0.65, 0.68, 0.68, 0.65, 0.61, 0.55, 0.45, 0.3, 0.13.
Ramp-up (10 to 90 % of peak) 0.15-0.46 s, typical 0.28 s. Ramp-down 0.23-0.58 s, typical 0.47 s.
Peak speed about 39-69 % of the frame width per second (median 54), measured as median pixel motion.
rules.ours_now: ramp-up 0.17 s, ramp-down 0.4 s, peak 45 % per second. Close, a little too abrupt at the start.
rules.unit_note: speed here = median pixel motion of the whole frame (ref_look.py); CAM-02 peak speed is the edge motion of the fitted camera model, so its numbers are larger.

rules.observed: The left and right edge strips are softer than the centre in 24-61 % of frames (median 35 %), edge sharpness 0.41-0.73 of the centre. Sharpness during a flight is the same as during a hold (ratio 1.05).
rules.rule: Use depth of field at the frame edges (soft foreground objects), not motion blur.
rules.why: A soft near object at the edge pushes the subject back in depth and costs nothing while the camera moves.
do: Put an out-of-focus foreground object (post, rope, leaf, rail, shoulder) at the left or right edge in about a third of the shots.
Keep edge sharpness 0.4-0.7 of centre sharpness.
No global motion blur.
rules.ours_now: edge 0.82 of centre, soft edges in 20 % of frames

rules.estimate_note: line width is accurate to about 1 px; head finder only works on clean near-white heads (4-78 found per video)
rules.observed: Heads are 0.1236-0.2064 (median 0.171) of the frame height (diameter), line width of outlines and limbs 0.0053-0.0106 (median 0.0065) of the frame width, outline thickness about 0.0381-0.1569 (median 0.057) of the head diameter, uneven around the head (std/mean 0.5206-0.9042 (median 0.737)).
rules.rule: Draw characters big with a thick uneven outline.
rules.why: A big head and a heavy hand-drawn outline make the character readable on a phone and give it the house look.
do: Median head diameter about 17 % of frame height (12-21 %): frame characters closer than a wide shot most of the time.
Outline line width about 0.65 % of the frame width (0.5-1.1 %), i.e. 7 px at 1080 wide; heavier on the head than on the limbs.
Vary the outline width around the head by about +-70 % of its mean (std/mean 0.5-0.9) instead of one even stroke.
Eyes: diameter about 22 % of the head diameter, centred at 50 % of the head height (where eyes are open dots).
rules.ours_now: head 13 % of frame height, line width 0.53 % of frame width

rules.observed: Share of the picture by surface: flat colour 0.3498-0.4774 (median 0.42), smooth gradient 0.1414-0.1952 (median 0.176), detailed surface 0.1254-0.1976 (median 0.162), hard edge 0.188-0.3068 (median 0.234). Ours: flat 0.60, gradient 0.056, detailed 0.093.
rules.rule: No big surface stays a single flat colour. Give every wall, floor and sky a gradient plus one texture or noise layer.
rules.why: Gradients and fine texture are what make the references look rich; flat fills look like a cheap game.
do: Flat colour at most about 45 % of the picture, smooth gradient 14-20 %, detailed surface 12-20 %.
Sky and walls: vertical or radial gradient. Floors: gradient plus a pattern (planks, tiles, carpet). Add rim light and a soft vignette.
Keep hard edges (outlines and text) at 19-31 % of the picture.

numbers.method: 5x5 local spread of grey values at 270x480: <1.5 flat, 1.5-4 smooth, 4-12 detailed, >12 edge

rules.ours_now: flat 0.60, gradient 0.056

rules.observed: Saturated warm colours cover 0.1416-0.6904 (median 0.442) of the picture and saturated cool colours 0.088-0.567 (median 0.346); together 42-97 % (median about 78 %). Warm-led: slot_machines, idea_zone, memory_price. Cool-led: grave_bell, roller_coasters.
rules.rule: Pick a warm-led or cool-led palette from the mood, but always show both: the second family is the accent.
rules.why: Warm against cool gives contrast without black; the references are colourful almost everywhere.
do: Saturated colours should cover about 80 % of the picture (not less than about 55 %).
Night or calm: cool base (60 % cool) with warm lamps and windows. Danger, money, crowds: warm base with cool shadows.
rules.ours_now: warm 0.29, cool 0.27: only 56 % saturated colour

rules.estimate_note: text height is reliable only in videos where the caption box is a single word (8 of 17); in the others white scenery in the band inflates it
rules.observed: One word at a time, 1.928-2.592 (median 2.39) words per second, each word stays about 0.33-0.382 (median 0.37) s, shown 100 % of the time, centred at 0.6758-0.704 (median 0.699) of the frame height. A word is about 3-4 % of the frame height and 25-30 % of the frame width. It pops: the first 3 frames are 1.0292-1.206 (median 1.113) times the steady height.
rules.rule: Burn in captions: one spoken word at a time, big white text with a dark outline, centred low, popping in.
rules.why: Viewers watch without sound; one word at a time keeps the eye on the centre of the screen.
do: One word per caption, shown from the word's start to the next word's start (about 0.37 s).
Position: centred horizontally, centre at 70 % of the frame height.
Height of a one-word caption about 3.5 % of the frame height; white fill, dark outline about 15 % of the letter height.
Pop: start 10-15 % larger and settle to normal within 3 frames.
rules.ours_now: our engine draws no captions

rules.estimate_note: estimate: jitter left after removing a 9-frame running mean of the camera shift; fast whips can also show up
rules.observed: Shake events per minute 2.86-19.7 (median 9.7), amplitude about 0.804-1.67 (median 1.06) % of frame width, they die out in 0.118-0.282 (median 0.17) s. Ours: 35 per minute that die in 0.03 s.
rules.rule: Shake the camera only on impacts, a few times a minute, and let it ring out for about 0.17 s.
rules.why: Rare shake sells the hit; constant jitter reads as a cheap handheld effect.
do: 3-20 shakes per minute (median 10), each about 1 % of frame width, decaying over 0.12-0.28 s.
Put them on the impact word or the hit frame, not on every cut.
rules.ours_now: 35 per minute, decay 0.03 s

rules.observed: Scene changes fall within 0.12 s of a sound onset in 0.5494-0.861 (median 0.679) of cases, but so would random times: lift over chance 0.85-1.258 (median 1.02) (about 1.0). Shakes: lift 0.722-1.372 (median 0.99).
rules.rule: Do not snap scene changes to voice onsets. Tie picture to the MEANING of the word (the noun appears when it is spoken).
rules.why: The voice has a new onset every 0.4 s, so onset alignment is automatic; what viewers notice is that the thing named is on screen.
do: Show each named object within about 0.3 s of the word (script-match check).
Music, voice and sound effects cannot be separated reliably from the mixed track; sound-effect timing is NOT measured.

rules.rule: Choose the picture from what the WORDS are doing (their intent), not only from the nouns they name.
do: Give every beat one intent: hook, introduce_place_or_time, introduce_character, explain_mechanism, give_number_or_quantity, physical_action, create_suspense, surprising_reveal, emotional_reaction, dialogue_or_argument, time_passes, comedic_beat, crowd_or_scale, summarize_or_conclude.

Pick the shot recipe (S01-S08) and the camera purpose from the intent, the assets that exist and the previous beat. Several recipes are allowed per intent (see intent_map); there is no fixed order of shots.
A number, a mechanism, a reaction and a place reveal must not get the same kind of shot.
rules.why: SCR-02 says show every noun; this says HOW to show it depends on what the sentence does.
evidence: chatgpt script_to_shot_mapping (9 intents), merged with our situations (hook, time passes, comedy, crowd, dialogue)
rules.ours_now: Gemini shot notes pick a camera move per shot but have no intent field; the PLAYBOOK situations are used only by Gemini reading prose.
rules.reconciled_with: SCR-02, SCR-04, PRF-04 and the situation recipes stay as they are; intent_map links them.

rules.rule: Every camera choice has a written purpose, and a HOLD is a choice too. There is no default of moving and no default of holding.
do: Write the purpose first: establish, reveal, follow, inspect, emphasize, compare, land_on_prop, power_angle, hold_for_performance, carry_to_next_place, impact.
Then pick the move (or static). A move needs a start view, an end view, a duration and an ease; a hold needs a reason (CAM-13).
Keep the mix of CAM-01 (flights 27-54 % of the time) as the reference; do not force more stillness or more motion than the story needs.
rules.why: ChatGPT said hold-first; our measurements show 15-24 flights per minute. Purpose-first satisfies both: the mix comes out of the purposes.
rules.ours_now: camera keys in story.js have no purpose; Gemini writes a free-text camera line per shot.
rules.reconciled_with: CAM-01 (measured mix) stays the numeric reference. CAM-13 lists when not to move.

rules.rule: Declare the composition of every shot: one primary subject, secondary context, a focal point, and a caption-clear zone.
do: Primary subject and hero object must be readable at phone size (about 360 px wide).
Keep key content out of the caption band: captions sit at about 70 % of frame height (CAP-01), so the default clear zone is x 0.1-0.9, y 0.62-0.78.
Put the focal point where the viewer should look after the camera lands (rule of thirds is a start, not a rule).
rules.why: The planner and the preview check need a place to measure from.
rules.ours_now: none: composition is implicit in camera keys; nothing declares or checks it.
rules.reconciled_with: CONTRADICTION: ChatGPT proposed the caption safe zone y 0.78-0.95. Our measured caption band is about 70 % (CAP-01, CAP-02). We keep ours.

rules.rule: Lock each character, object and place once, and keep it the same in every beat unless the script changes it.
do: Write an identity lock per character: head shape, hat, outfit colours, skin, beard, outline weight, size.
Keep scale, screen side (who stands left or right) and position between beats of one place; change them only in a beat that lists continuity_change.
When a story changes a look on purpose (boss face turns purple, rail heats up) list it as continuity_change.
rules.why: Identity from headwear and clothes (CHR-02) only works if it does not drift between shots.
rules.ours_now: cast is defined by Gemini in cast.js per project; nothing checks that beats keep it.
rules.reconciled_with: CHR-02 stays; this adds the lock and the screen-side rule.

rules.rule: Play an action in order: attention (gaze), anticipation, action, contact, response, settle. Gaze leads the hand.
do: Eyes move first to the target, then the arm, then the hand touches.
Give the body a small wind-up before a big action and a settle after it.
Keep small-talk beats quiet: blink, breath, a small gesture only when the words need it.
Our kit has one face name per beat and fixed arm poses (no separate brow, pupil, mouth channels): use the closest face and pose, and say so.
rules.why: FX-01 says anticipation, action, follow-through; this adds gaze and the contact and response steps.
rules.ours_now: idle() and blinkAt() exist in kit/engine/motion.js; M.anticip exists; no gaze-leads-hand logic; one face channel only.
rules.reconciled_with: Extends FX-01. Limited by roman.js: no separate brow/pupil/mouth channels.

rules.rule: Show a physical event as a cause chain: start state, force, path, contact, response, settle. Add the secondary effects that belong to it.
do: Name the contact target. Add only fitting effects: debris, dust, smoke, sparks, splash, recoil, a camera kick (FX-05), a sound (SND-03).
Time them: effects start on the contact frame, not before.
rules.why: PHY-01 says things have weight; this makes the chain checkable.
rules.ours_now: fx cards exist (fxDebris, fxSmoke, fxGlow in kit/engine/roman.js); chains are written by hand per scene.

rules.rule: Give each kind of thing its own motion: rigid, elastic, fluid, smoke, flame, rope with lag. Do not move everything at one speed.
do: Smoke rises and spreads, water flows in waves, flame flickers, rope lags behind its anchor, rigid things do not wobble.
Name the motion_profile of an object event in the beat plan.
rules.why: Uniform motion reads as fake.
rules.ours_now: fxSmoke, fxMotes, fxDebris exist; each has its own simple timing; no shared profile list.

rules.rule: Each material has its own shape and shading language (see material_recipes M01-M07).
do: Wood: planks and seams with a grain direction. Metal: edge highlights and dark seams. Stone: block variation. Earth: layered strata and pebbles. Water: ripples and a bright glint. Foliage: clumps with value variation. Glass: reflection and a thin edge.
Choose the materials per place in the beat plan (material_ids), not per shot.
rules.why: Surfaces with real texture are a measured need (COL-02, WLD-02); this says which texture.
rules.ours_now: toonbase/paint.js and the railroads_v2 world.js have texture helpers (woodTex, sandTex, gravelTex, strataTex in mine/railroads_v2/web/main.js); no material list in the kit.
rules.reconciled_with: WLD-02 and COL-02 (measured) say that big surfaces are never flat; this says what each material looks like.

rules.rule: Big forms first, then a few purposeful details. Do not add small noise everywhere.
do: Silhouette and big structure must read first.
Add 3-5 details per hero object that say what it is: seams, bolts, labels, bevels, grain, wear.
rules.why: Detail should help the story, not hide it.
rules.ours_now: hand-built per project.
rules.reconciled_with: COL-02 still applies: gradient plus fine grain on every big surface (measured). MAT-02 limits the storytelling details, not the base surface.

rules.rule: One motivated key light direction per place, the same on people, props and ground, with contact shadows.
do: Choose the key (sun, window, lamp) and keep its side in every shot of that place.
Soft contact shadow under every person and hero object (CHR-03).
rules.why: A different light side on a character and its set breaks the cartoon world.
rules.ours_now: applyLight()/placeSun() in kit/engine/main.js give one sun per place; cards get skin tint from the light; the key side is not checked.

rules.rule: Use one practical glow, rim or spotlight to say what to look at. Do not glow everything.
do: The glow marks the thing the words are about (hot rail, bomb timer, coin).
If everything glows, nothing is the subject.
rules.why: Directs attention.
rules.ours_now: fxGlow and LK.bloom-like effects exist; used by hand.
rules.reconciled_with: LIT-04 (light effects as scenery: bloom on lamps, windows, sun) is scenery; LIT-06 is about the subject.

rules.rule: Sound effects are a separate track tied to picture events. The loudest sound lands on the key action; music stays under the voice.
do: List audio events per beat with a trigger: a word, an animation event or a transition.
Put an effect on the event frame (impact, appear, transition), not at the start of the word.
Keep the existing mix: music and effects at 50 % of the voice, loudness about -14 LUFS (SND-01).
rules.why: SND-02 says do not snap scene changes to voice onsets; effects follow picture events, not voice.
rules.ours_now: audio.py is written by Gemini per project from the SFX lines; mix.py does the levels.
rules.reconciled_with: ChatGPT audio peaks are amplitude only and unlabelled: not used as numbers.

rules.rule: Check before you render: make a small preview of every beat and judge it against the quality gates, then fix or reject bad beats before the full render.
do: One low-resolution frame per beat (start, middle, end) in a contact sheet.
Run the gates Q01-Q10 (rules.json quality_gates): some are automatic, some need Gemini vision, some need a person.
Do not start a full render while a gate marked automatic fails.
rules.why: A full render costs minutes to hours; a preview costs seconds.
rules.ours_now: partly: tools/gen_api.py renders 3 stills per shot and asks Gemini for PASS/FAIL (Gemini projects only, does not use beats or the gates Q01-Q10). frame_qa.py, ref_measure.py compare and ref_study.py compare run only AFTER the full render.
rules.reconciled_with: Extends CHK-01..13 (post-render checks) with pre-render checks.

rules.rule: For a new topic keep the universal habits (PRF-01) and choose the topic things fresh: place, props, materials, light, motion.
do: Never reuse a reference layout, prop set or shot order. Take the habit (how a reveal is built), not the picture.
Pick the topic profile (PRF-02, PRF-03) by what the story does: machine, money, mind, night.
rules.why: The goal is a toolkit for new topics, not a copy of 17 videos.
rules.ours_now: tested once: Why Perfect Railroads Don't Work (railroads_v2) from words only.
rules.reconciled_with: Overlaps PRF-01..03; the new part is the ban on copying layouts.

rules.rule: Choose how each thing is built by what the camera does to it: people are 2D cards in a 3D world, hero objects the camera moves around are 3D, far scenery can be flat layers, effects are billboards.
do: Orbit or close-up on it -> 3D mesh. Always front-facing -> 2D card. Far and static -> 2.5D layer. Smoke, sparks, glow -> billboard fx.
Write the representation per object in the beat plan.
rules.why: Keeps cost and look under control.
rules.ours_now: our kit already works this way (roman.js cards in a three.js world); the choice is made by hand.
rules.reconciled_with: Matches the existing kit; this is a decision guide, not a new engine.

steps: First flight starts within 1 s.
Close on a reacting face, main prop or place visible.
First flight ends on the hero object by 1.5-3 s.
Start tight on a detail or face.
Fly out, up or around 0.8-1.6 s with ease in and out.
End on a wide with the hero object, a far landmark and 6-10 dressing pieces.
Hold 0.5-1 s.
Medium shot, character readable by hat and clothes.
Expression first, then a prop in the hand.
Slow creep.
Fast push that decelerates onto the prop on the word.
Prop fills 40-100 % of the frame, text readable.
Light effect on it (glow, glass highlight, bloom).
Two-shot or close-up held.
Camera creeps under 8 % per second.
Face changes every 1-1.5 s.
Anticipation hold 0.6 s.
Push to the point of action with streaks or starburst.
Debris 0.5-1 s.
Pull back, bystander reaction within 0.2 s.
Crane to top-down to show the layout.
Draw the idea in the world (ring, arcs, numbers).
Come back down to a character reacting.
Change the colour grade on the cut or the dissolve.
Face shows the new feeling with its effect (steam, sweat, tears).
Dissolve with ghost.
Show a clock, calendar, ledger or season change.
Light changes with the time.
Wide from low or high.
Hundreds of tiny varied people in rows, bunting, a few animated.
Cut or fly to one face in the crowd.
Low angle, big prop in the foreground.
Hard long shadows, orange low light.
Hold, then a sudden push.
Land a hard beat first (impact, fall, reveal).
Cut or push to the gag picture: knocked-out face stamped in a sand ring, exaggerated stare, size contrast.
Hold 1-1.5 s with only a small motion (dust settling, eye twitch).
Return to the first place or object.
Slow pull back, final line on the prop or a face.
Medium shot, character beside the big number prop, camera holds (CAM-13).
On the key word push toward the prop and land on it with the number readable (CAM-05).
The number changes on the spoken word (counter rolls, panel light turns on).
Fly out or up to show what the number means in the world (skyline, crowd, line of people).

checks.what: hard cuts per minute
scene changes per minute (new place or set-up, incl. dissolves)
hard cuts should be well below scene changes (angle cuts inside a scene)
share of shots that are only a zoom
share of time the picture moves fast
depth parallax in flights
palette size (4-bit colours over 0.5 %)
frame-to-frame change (median)
script match: every noun of each sentence appears within 0.3 s of the word
checks.tool: manual until the script-match check is built (step 2)

checks.what: hard cuts that are not scene changes, per minute
share of scene changes that are hard cuts
flat-colour share of the picture
checks.tool: python3 kit/tools/ref_look.py study video.mp4 --name X --group ours

checks.what: captions on screen (share of time)

engine.note: Nothing from rules.json is wired into kit/engine yet. v2.2 (bomb story) tests whether the rules help when applied by hand in story.js. Update this list only when code reads a rule or a number.
known_gaps_in_our_engine_found_by_measur: no burned-in captions at all (references show one word at a time for 100 % of the time)
scene changes are 100 % hard cuts: no dissolve, no fly-through scene change
25 hard cuts per minute inside scenes (references median 1.1)
surfaces too flat: 60 % flat colour, 5.6 % smooth gradient (references 35-48 % and 14-20 %)
heads small: 13 % of frame height (references 12-21 %, median 17 %) and skin-coloured, not near-white
shake: 35 events per minute that die in 0.03 s (references 3-20 per minute, 0.12-0.28 s)
camera ease: ramp-up 0.17 s, no long ease-out (references ramp-up 0.28 s, ramp-down 0.47 s)

origin.our_measured: computed by our tools from the reference videos
origin.our_observed: read by eye from frames by Claude
origin.chatgpt: proposed by the independent ChatGPT study bundle (2026-11-08)

values.measured: numbers in the rule were measured
values.designed: starting values chosen by a person or model, not measured

provenance_key.production_tested: none | hand_applied (applied by hand in a project and measured) | code_tested (read by render code and measured). Details per rule: kit/reference/knowledge/traceability.json

shot_recipes.name: Establishing world
shot_recipes.purpose: Orient viewer to location, scale and key objects
shot_recipes.framing: wide or medium-wide; clear horizon / ground plane; one obvious focal point
shot_recipes.camera_options: hold or slow purposeful pan/dolly only if it reveals geography (starting suggestion; CAM-16 decides: a move needs a purpose, a hold needs a reason)
shot_recipes.motion: ambient environment motion plus subtle character action
shot_recipes.transition_hint: cut/dissolve/fly-through only if it conveys a location change
shot_recipes.typical_seconds_status: designed starting range from the ChatGPT bundle; our measured scene length is a median of 2.4 s with the camera and dissolves carrying changes (CUT-02), so tune per beat

shot_recipes.name: Narrator character hold
shot_recipes.purpose: Let the narration land while maintaining character presence
shot_recipes.framing: medium / medium-wide; character readable; supporting set dressing
shot_recipes.camera_options: locked or nearly locked (starting suggestion; CAM-16 decides: a move needs a purpose, a hold needs a reason)
shot_recipes.motion: blink, breath, small hand gesture or gaze shift only when motivated
shot_recipes.typical_seconds_status: designed starting range from the ChatGPT bundle; our measured scene length is a median of 2.4 s with the camera and dissolves carrying changes (CUT-02), so tune per beat

shot_recipes.name: Object / mechanism insert
shot_recipes.purpose: Explain a mechanism, detail or evidence
shot_recipes.framing: close-up, top-down, POV or cutaway; object fills enough of frame to read
shot_recipes.camera_options: locked, short push or tracking move that follows the mechanism (starting suggestion; CAM-16 decides: a move needs a purpose, a hold needs a reason)
shot_recipes.motion: show component state changes in causal order
shot_recipes.transition_hint: return to wider context after explanation
shot_recipes.typical_seconds_status: designed starting range from the ChatGPT bundle; our measured scene length is a median of 2.4 s with the camera and dissolves carrying changes (CUT-02), so tune per beat

shot_recipes.name: Character reaction close-up
shot_recipes.purpose: Emphasize recognition, fear, surprise, confidence or realization
shot_recipes.framing: head / upper body; eyebrows, pupils and mouth readable
shot_recipes.camera_options: cut to close-up or short push; avoid continuous generic zoom (starting suggestion; CAM-16 decides: a move needs a purpose, a hold needs a reason)
shot_recipes.motion: gaze, brow and mouth lead the pose; settle before next beat
shot_recipes.typical_seconds_status: designed starting range from the ChatGPT bundle; our measured scene length is a median of 2.4 s with the camera and dissolves carrying changes (CUT-02), so tune per beat

shot_recipes.name: Scale reveal / pullback
shot_recipes.purpose: Reveal crowd, full machine, geography or surprising scale
shot_recipes.framing: start with partial/close view; end with the full subject/context visible
shot_recipes.camera_options: crane / dolly back / zoom only if perspective is not needed; use parallax when possible (starting suggestion; CAM-16 decides: a move needs a purpose, a hold needs a reason)
shot_recipes.motion: keep the focal subject anchored until reveal completes
shot_recipes.transition_hint: hold the revealed composition long enough to read
shot_recipes.typical_seconds_status: designed starting range from the ChatGPT bundle; our measured scene length is a median of 2.4 s with the camera and dissolves carrying changes (CUT-02), so tune per beat

shot_recipes.name: Action demonstration
shot_recipes.purpose: Show how an action works and its consequence
shot_recipes.framing: wide enough to understand actor, prop and destination; insert details where needed
shot_recipes.camera_options: track/follow only if subject travels; maintain screen direction (starting suggestion; CAM-16 decides: a move needs a purpose, a hold needs a reason)
shot_recipes.transition_hint: cut to impact or consequence only when it clarifies causality
shot_recipes.typical_seconds_status: designed starting range from the ChatGPT bundle; our measured scene length is a median of 2.4 s with the camera and dissolves carrying changes (CUT-02), so tune per beat

shot_recipes.name: Diagrammatic metaphor / cutaway
shot_recipes.framing: clean isolated diagram or transparent/cutaway body/object; simple composition
shot_recipes.camera_options: hold or subtle drift; avoid busy movement (starting suggestion; CAM-16 decides: a move needs a purpose, a hold needs a reason)
shot_recipes.motion: animate only the relevant concept (flow, balls, gauges, connections)
shot_recipes.typical_seconds_status: designed starting range from the ChatGPT bundle; our measured scene length is a median of 2.4 s with the camera and dissolves carrying changes (CUT-02), so tune per beat

shot_recipes.name: Two-character dialogue
shot_recipes.framing: balanced two-shot; both faces readable; props placed between/near them
shot_recipes.camera_options: hold; change to close-up only when reaction matters (starting suggestion; CAM-16 decides: a move needs a purpose, a hold needs a reason)
shot_recipes.motion: alternating gaze, one speaker gesture, listener reaction
shot_recipes.typical_seconds_status: designed starting range from the ChatGPT bundle; our measured scene length is a median of 2.4 s with the camera and dissolves carrying changes (CUT-02), so tune per beat

hook.note: candidates, not a sequence: the planner scores them against assets, the previous beat and CAM-10 (vary the moves)

introduce_place_or_time.note: candidates, not a sequence: the planner scores them against assets, the previous beat and CAM-10 (vary the moves)

introduce_character.required_visuals: The character readable by hat and clothes, expression first.
introduce_character.note: candidates, not a sequence: the planner scores them against assets, the previous beat and CAM-10 (vary the moves)

explain_mechanism.required_visuals: The hero object, its moving part and the cause and effect state.
explain_mechanism.note: candidates, not a sequence: the planner scores them against assets, the previous beat and CAM-10 (vary the moves)

physical_action.note: candidates, not a sequence: the planner scores them against assets, the previous beat and CAM-10 (vary the moves)

material_recipes.shape_language: planks, beams, posts, boards with clear seams and slightly softened edges
material_recipes.surface: subtle grain direction, value variation, occasional knots/wear; do not over-noise
material_recipes.lighting: broad warm highlight and soft contact shadow
material_recipes.status: production recipe inferred from visible stylized wood surfaces
material_recipes.note: shape-and-shading checklist inferred by ChatGPT from stylized surfaces; not measured

material_recipes.shape_language: simple bevelled plates, rims, bolts, hinges, rods and cylindrical forms

quality_gates.pass_condition: Head proportions, face placement, costume, outline and accessories remain consistent across planned shots.

checks.what: character ids, outfit, hat and identity_lock are the same in every beat
head, face, costume look the same across the preview frames
final approval of the look

quality_gates.pass_condition: One primary focal subject; key action and hero object readable at phone scale; caption safe zone does not obscure critical content.

checks.what: the focal point is not inside the caption clear zone (warning); the zone defaults to the measured caption band
hero object and action readable at phone size in the preview frames
checks.implemented_in: existing, partly: tools/gen_api.py shot phase (Gemini PASS/FAIL on 3 stills per shot against MUST SEE / MUST NOT, Gemini projects only); not run on beats; accuracy untested

checks.what: does the picture say what the words say

quality_gates.pass_condition: Every non-static move has a written purpose, target, direction, duration and easing. HOLD is allowed.

checks.what: every beat has a camera purpose and mode; a move has duration, ease and from/to; a hold has a rationale
the move helps the story

quality_gates.pass_condition: Every sentence/beat has an explicit visual purpose and subject; no generic filler shots.

checks.what: beat words joined equal the narration; word ranges cover all words in order; beat times follow the word times
checks.implemented_in: validate_beats.py (implemented); make_notes.py checks the words for the shot notes

checks.what: each named noun is visible within 0.3 s of its word (CHK-07)
checks.implemented_in: existing, partly: tools/gen_api.py shot phase (Gemini PASS/FAIL on 3 stills per shot against MUST SEE / MUST NOT, Gemini projects only); not run on beats; accuracy untested

quality_gates.pass_condition: Object has initial state, action/force, trajectory, contact/response and settled state; no teleporting or weightless motion.

checks.what: physical events name a contact target and fitting secondary effects
the motion looks causal and has weight

quality_gates.pass_condition: Foreground/midground/background, scale cues, contact shadows and perspective relationships are present where relevant.

checks.what: every environment declares foreground, midground, background
parallax and soft-edge share on rendered frames
checks.implemented_in: existing, after rendering: kit/tools/ref_study.py compare, ref_look.py

quality_gates.pass_condition: Wood/metal/stone/water/cloth/glass read differently by geometry and shading, not colour alone.

checks.what: every declared material id exists in material_recipes
the surface reads as that material in the preview
checks.implemented_in: existing, partly: tools/gen_api.py shot phase (Gemini PASS/FAIL on 3 stills per shot against MUST SEE / MUST NOT, Gemini projects only); not run on beats; accuracy untested

quality_gates.pass_condition: Cuts and transitions correspond to semantic changes; adjacent shots do not repeat the same information.

checks.what: every beat has a transition type and reason (frames for dissolve, fly-through, flash); hard cuts at most 45 % of scene changes (CHK-11) and at least one dissolve (warnings)
each cut is on a meaning beat

quality_gates.pass_condition: SFX are linked to named visual events, and narration remains intelligible over music.

checks.what: audio events have a valid trigger and fall inside the beat; word triggers point at real words
mix level and loudness
sound quality and taste

quality_gates.pass_condition: Low-resolution animatic and contact sheet reviewed before a full-resolution render.

checks.what: all ids resolve; every required asset is declared; beats cover the whole video without gaps or overlaps
a build check of the real code (assets render, no errors)
